items.title: Fact Check: Post claiming inhaling of steam with turmeric, pepper, lemon, ginger, basil will kill corona virus is not true
items.snippet_en: Vishvas News found a viral social media post claiming that inhaling steam from boiled turmeric, pepper, lemon, peeled ginger, and basil seven times would kill the coronavirus to be false.

items.title: Lemon Juice Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel, or Anywhere Else - FactCheck.org
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org debunks a false claim that a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice would eliminate the novel coronavirus. An infectious diseases physician stated there is no data showing that lemon juice or hot tea would kill a virus.

items.title: Facebook Messenger video falsely claims hot lemon juice can kill the coronavirus
items.snippet_en: Politifact states there is no scientific evidence that lemon can treat or prevent the coronavirus, and health officials have debunked the claim. The WHO recommends fruits and vegetables for health, but not lemon for COVID-19.

items.title: Will Drinking Lemon Juice Kill The Coronavirus? Dr. Mallika Marshall Answers Your Questions
items.snippet_en: Dr. Mallika Marshall states that consuming acidic liquids like lemon juice will not kill the coronavirus.

items.title: Can drinking or gargling with lemon juice or lemon water kill the coronavirus? Short answer: No
items.snippet_en: A Facebook post clarifies that drinking lemon juice or water will not kill COVID-19 or protect against it. The theory that COVID-19 cannot live in acidic environments is incorrect, as the virus can survive in acidic conditions.

items.title: False claims that drinking water with lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online | Fact Check
items.snippet_en: AFP reports that experts found no proof that drinking warm water with lemon is effective in preventing COVID-19. Henry Chenal stated that consuming high amounts of vitamin C has never proven effective against coronavirus.
